reason: Section 18 is current despite one repealed subsection and contains three target-grounded registration workflow topics: receipt/examination/rejection, certificate or notice consequences, and later rejection/amendment/discretionary registration rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Instrument record, examination, acceptance, and rejection

evidenceText: assign a registration number, date and time
record of the acceptance of the instrument
accepted for registration
may refuse to file or register and may reject an instrument

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 18(1) through 18(4) cover the registrar's first-stage instrument record, examination, acceptance, registration, and rejection grounds.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the registrar records, examines, accepts, registers, or rejects an instrument under section 18.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certificates, Registry Act notice, and parcel identification

evidenceText: cancel the certificate of registered ownership
issue to the owner
issue and record under the Registry Act a notice
identified by its approved parcel identifier

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 18(5) through 18(7) address certificate actions, Registry Act notice after certain title registrations, and approved parcel identifier requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what certificate, notice, and parcel identifier actions follow specified registrations under section 18.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rejection notice, amending instruments, and discretionary Registry Act document registration

evidenceText: enter in the instrument record a record of the rejection
memorandum of the reasons for such rejection
shall notify the person who presented the instrument
shall not reject an instrument referred to in subsection 12(10)
be amended by the filing or registration of an amending instrument
may, in his absolute discretion, order the proper registrar to register it under this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The later usable subsections cover rejection records and notice, an exception to rejection, amending instruments, and discretionary registration of certain Registry Act documents; subsection 18(8) is repealed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the later section 18 rules for rejection records and notice, exceptions to rejection, amending instruments, and discretionary registration of Registry Act documents.

reason: Section 125 is a large regulation-making provision whose study grouping should follow the target's own regulation subjects, application/effect rules, subdivision-public-purpose rules, and pre-making/filing requirements.

prescribing the location, layout, equipment, standards and licensing of mobile home parks
respecting the subdividing of land
respecting development approvals
respecting land use and development policies

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 125(1) lists the main planning and development matters that may be regulated.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the major planning, subdivision, development approval, building, and land use policy subjects that may be regulated under subsection 125(1).

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Area designation, effectiveness, inconsistency, and development officer rules

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 125 controls where regulations apply, when they are effective, how land use policy regulations prevail, and which bodies exercise development or zoning powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision public-purpose land, money, procedure, summary, and filing rules

evidenceText: the setting aside of land for public purposes
sections 79 and 80 apply with the necessary modifications

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall section 125's subdivision public-purpose land and money rules, the procedure before making regulations, the written-summary rule, and filing of regulations in land registration offices.

reason: Section 10 has three target-grounded objection-hearing topics: delivering a written objection and triggering a hearing, the no-objection decision path, and hearing parties plus notice contents.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Objection delivery and required hearing

evidenceText: written statement setting out the reasons for and any grounds and arguments
Registrar General shall hold a hearing to determine the validity of the objection

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10(1) and 10(2) describe how an objection is delivered and the hearing required after a timely written objection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an objection to boundary confirmation is delivered and when it requires the Registrar General to hold a hearing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No-objection confirmation or hearing decision

evidenceText: If no written statement of objection is delivered
confirm the location of the boundary or boundaries
hold a hearing in accordance with this Act and the regulations

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 10(3) gives the Registrar General a separate path when no written objection is delivered by the deadline.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Registrar General's options when no written objection is delivered.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Hearing parties and notice contents

evidenceText: are parties to a hearing held under this section
shall cause a notice of hearing to be given
shall specify the date, time and place of the hearing

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10(4) through 10(6) identify hearing parties and the required notice of hearing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who is a party to a section 10 hearing and what the hearing notice must contain.

reason: The target is a definitions section with six actual defined terms, and the groups should be organized only around terms defined in the target.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Coordinate monument and coordinate survey system definitions

evidenceText: coordinate monument” means a brass, bronze or aluminum cap or plate
coordinate survey system” means a system established under section 2

proposedGroups.reason: These two target definitions describe coordinate survey infrastructure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what coordinate monument and coordinate survey system mean under the Surveys Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corner and legal monument definitions

evidenceText: corner” means a point in an intersection of boundaries of land
legal monument” means a device planted by a surveyor

proposedGroups.reason: These target definitions identify boundary points and physical survey monuments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what corner and legal monument mean under the Surveys Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Survey and surveyor definitions

evidenceText: survey” means a survey to define the boundaries of land
surveyor” means a New Brunswick Land Surveyor

proposedGroups.reason: These target definitions identify the activity and the professional actor.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what survey and surveyor mean under the Surveys Act.

reason: Section 49.1 is a compact standalone rule defining regulator for the section and allowing a non-party regulator to assist the Board in a proceeding.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulator assistance to the Board without party status

evidenceText: regulator” means a regulator as defined in the Financial and Consumer Services Commission Act
may render assistance to the Board without becoming a party to the proceedings
may receive and accept information from the regulator that it considers relevant

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections work together: one defines regulator for section 49.1 and the other states how a regulator may assist the Board without becoming a party.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who is a regulator for section 49.1 and how that regulator may assist the Energy and Utilities Board without party status.

co-operate with

reason: Section 19 has several target-grounded registration topics: voidness against purchasers or creditors, exceptions or special timing rules, and transfer-affidavit forwarding; repealed subsections are not selected.

deemed fraudulent and void as against any bona fide judgment creditor

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when unregistered instruments are deemed fraudulent and void against purchasers or judgment creditors.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lease, official-sale, sheriff-sale, and will registration timing exceptions

if registered within six months after the day of its execution
A will registered within six months after the death of the testator

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special registration exceptions and timing rules for leases, sale conveyances, sheriff conveyances, and wills.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transfer affidavit requirement and forwarding
